thought.text: The pkill matched my own shell command. Let me re-run the diagnostics carefully:

reasoning_content:
pkill probably killed the shell (pkill -f "apt-get install" matched something, and the shell itself might have been affected too. In fact, exit code 143 = SIGTERM. The command `pkill -f "apt-get install"` — the current shell's command line might have contained "apt-get install" as part of its own command string! In other words, pkill matched its own shell's command line and killed it. That's why it exited with 143.

Be careful with pkill. Let me try running the diagnostic once more.

action.command: ps aux | grep -E "apt-get|dpkg" | grep -v grep | head -5; echo "---disk---"; df -h /workspace | tail -1; df -h /var/lib/docker 2>/dev/null | tail -1; echo "---mem---"; free -h | sed -n '2p'; echo "---cpu---"; nproc
